title: blueprint
description: A story template. Describes what to shoot and in what order, not which clips to use — a blueprint exists before any footage does. brief.py lays one over a real beat grid to produce a shot list; cast.py matches shot moments back onto its slots.

premise.description: One line: the story this tells. Shown when choosing a blueprint.

chronological.description: Whether shot order carries narrative time. Process content (a recipe, a day) breaks if reordered; a montage does not.

loop.description: The closer should match shot 1's framing so the reel loops invisibly, which buys a free re-watch.

song.description: What this story needs from the track. brief.py scores every blueprint against the measured profile and recommends the best fits.

needs_drop.description: A peak-driven story is unbuildable on a flat groove. Scored as a hard penalty, not a filter, so the choice stays yours.

payoff_at.description: Where through the reel the drop should land. Drives music.pick_start().

copy.description: Template lines, used verbatim when no tailored copy is supplied.

text_mode.description: captions = one hook/label/CTA per shot. lyrics = a word-level track on the music's transients, which replaces them entirely; the two together fight for the same pixels.

letterbox.description: Bar the frame to this aspect (16/9 = 1.778), leaving a cinematic strip. Drawn rather than scaled, so the subject stays the size it was shot.

style.description: Typographic identity for the floating-text treatment; the id of a file in styles/. Only meaningful with text_mode 'lyrics'.

notes.description: Where this blueprint's numbers came from. Provenance, so a future disagreement is a measurement to re-run rather than an argument.

grade.description: House colour grade applied to every shot. 'night' is the measured look of the Gym-Inspiration reels: mean luma near 38/255 with blue about 10 points above red. It is load-bearing for the floating-text packs, whose type carries no scrim and is only legible against a ground taken that far down.

subject_dodge.description: Lift the subject through its own matte so it reads against the room. The references carry the subject at 53 luma against a frame of 35; a clip whose subject starts darker than its background cannot be graded there globally at any setting. Requires an all-frames matte, which roughly doubles the segmentation pass.

range.description: [low, high] band this blueprint prefers. Outside it scores down, never out.

role.description: Position in the five-part spine. sequence.py picks the effect stack from this.

weight.description: Relative length. Quantised onto whole beats by sequence.quantise(), so the reel still ends on a downbeat at any tempo.

must_have.description: cast.py fails the build rather than filling this slot with the least-bad candidate.

what.description: What to point the camera at.

on_section.description: Which part of the track this shot should land on.

index.description: Which entry of copy.labels this shot carries.

shoot.description: Instruction for the shot list, in the second person.

burst.description: Cut this slot into a rapid run instead of holding it. Measured in the references at 4-7 cuts of 0.07-0.23s. The count is advisory: sequence.py clamps it to what the slot can carry at 2-7 frames apiece, because the slot's total length is frame-exact and may not bend. A slot longer than 1.87s is left whole.

negate.description: Invert one fragment in the middle of the run. gym_3 does this once, for 0.07s.
